grammarPoint.title: Inversion after negative adverbials
grammarPoint.summary: Use inversion after negative adverbials at the beginning of a sentence to add emphasis, often in formal or literary contexts.
grammarPoint.explanation:
Inversion after negative adverbials is a grammatical structure used to create *emphasis* or a more *formal* and *dramatic* style. When a negative adverbial phrase (like "never," "rarely," "not only," "hardly," "under no circumstances") begins a sentence, the subject and auxiliary verb swap positions, similar to how they do in a question.

This structure is not common in everyday spoken English but is frequently found in written language, speeches, and formal declarations. It draws attention to the negative aspect of the statement, making it sound stronger and more impactful.

The inversion always involves an auxiliary verb (do/does/did, have/has/had, be, or a modal verb like can/could, will/would, should/must). If there is no auxiliary verb in the original statement, you must add "do," "does," or "did" before the subject, just like in a question.
patterns: Negative adverbial + auxiliary verb + subject + main verb
Not only + do/does/did + subject + base verb
Hardly/Scarcely + had + subject + past participle + when/before...
Under no circumstances + modal verb + subject + base verb

examples.text: Never have I seen such a breathtaking sunset.
examples.note: Emphasizes the uniqueness of the experience.

examples.text: Not only did she win the competition, but she also broke a world record.
Rarely do we encounter such complex problems in our research.
examples.note: Stresses the infrequency of difficult issues.

examples.text: Hardly had the concert started when the power went out.
examples.note: Shows one event immediately followed by another, with emphasis.

examples.text: Under no circumstances should you open that package.
examples.note: Gives a strong warning or prohibition.

commonErrors.wrong: Seldom I travel abroad for work.
commonErrors.right: Seldom do I travel abroad for work.
commonErrors.note: Remember to add an auxiliary verb (do/does/did) if there isn't one.

commonErrors.wrong: Not only she is talented, but she is also very kind.
commonErrors.right: Not only is she talented, but she is also very kind.
commonErrors.note: Invert the auxiliary verb and subject.

commonErrors.wrong: Never I have felt so relieved.
commonErrors.right: Never have I felt so relieved.
commonErrors.note: The auxiliary verb 'have' must come before the subject 'I'.

exercises.question: ___ had the train left the station when the passenger realized he had forgotten his wallet.
exercises.explanation: "No sooner... than" is a common inverted structure indicating one event immediately followed by another.

exercises.question: Under no circumstances ___ leave your belongings unattended.
exercises.explanation: After a negative adverbial like "Under no circumstances," the auxiliary verb (should) comes before the subject (you).

exercises.question: Not only ___ the project on time, but they also exceeded expectations.
exercises.explanation: "Not only" requires inversion with an auxiliary verb (did) before the subject (they) and the base form of the main verb (finish).

exercises.question: Little ___ about the true impact of the new policy.
exercises.explanation: "Little" as a negative adverbial requires inversion with "do" before the subject "we" and the base verb "know."

exercises.text: Rarely ___ I ___ such dedication from a team.
exercises.explanation: "Rarely" requires inversion with "do" and the base form of the main verb.

exercises.text: Not only ___ the company expand its market, but it also increased its profits.
exercises.explanation: "Not only" requires inversion with "did" for past simple tense.

exercises.text: Under no circumstances ___ you ___ your password.
exercises.explanation: "Under no circumstances" requires inversion with a modal verb like "should" before the subject, followed by the base verb.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: The negative adverbial "Never" at the start of the sentence triggers inversion of the auxiliary verb "have" and the subject "I".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: "Not only" at the beginning of the sentence requires inversion with the auxiliary "did" before the subject "he" and the base verb "apologize".

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: Seldom she visits her family in the countryside.
answers: Seldom does she visit her family in the countryside.
exercises.explanation: When "Seldom" begins a sentence, the auxiliary verb "does" must come before the subject "she".

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: Hardly they had finished the report when the deadline was extended.
answers: Hardly had they finished the report when the deadline was extended.
exercises.explanation: After "Hardly," the auxiliary verb "had" must be inverted with the subject "they."

exercises.source: She had never experienced such intense pressure before.
answers: Never had she experienced such intense pressure before.
exercises.explanation: Starting with the negative adverbial "Never" requires inversion of the auxiliary verb "had" and the subject "she."

exercises.source: You should not, under any circumstances, reveal this information.
exercises.instruction: Begin the sentence with "Under no circumstances."
answers: Under no circumstances should you reveal this information.
exercises.explanation: When "Under no circumstances" begins a sentence, the modal verb "should" must be inverted with the subject "you."
